# wrnty

> Track every warranty and receipt, get reminded before they expire, and export a claim-ready PDF — one-time purchase, no subscription.

wrnty is an iOS app for iPhone and iPad that keeps your product warranties and receipts organised, reminds you before each warranty expires, and lets you export a PDF pack for insurance and warranty claims. Your data stays on your device and syncs only through your own iCloud — there is no account and nothing is uploaded to the developer.

## Key Facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad, iOS 17+)
- Pricing: Free to track up to 2 warranties; Premium is a one-time in-app purchase (no subscription) for unlimited items, expiry alerts, iCloud sync and PDF export
- Privacy: no account required; data stored on-device and in the user's own iCloud; no ads, no tracking, no data selling; optional anonymous analytics that can be turned off; GDPR compliant
- Developer: 12F ApS, Denmark (https://12f.dk/)
- Website: https://wrnty.12f.dk/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wrnty-warranty-receipts/id6747742961

## Features

- Track warranties with product name, brand, merchant, price, purchase and expiry dates, serial number and notes
- Store receipts and documents as photos and PDFs
- Expiry reminders delivered to the Home and Lock Screen (Premium)
- Home and Lock Screen widgets showing what's expiring next
- Export warranties to PDF for insurance and warranty claims (Premium)
- iCloud sync across iPhone and iPad (Premium)
- Spotlight search to jump straight to a product from iOS search
- Organise by category, brand and purchase date; running total of covered value
- Dark mode, VoiceOver accessibility, and available in 28 languages

## Blog

Practical advice on warranties, receipts and buying smart, published at https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/ (RSS: https://wrnty.12f.dk/feed.xml).

- [What a warranty actually covers on phones, laptops and gadgets](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/what-your-warranty-actually-covers/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-31. Most people think a warranty covers everything that breaks.
- [What counts as proof of purchase — and what to do without a receipt](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/what-counts-as-proof-of-purchase/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-31. A warranty claim usually requires proof of purchase, but the receipt is only one acceptable form.
- [Consumer rights when something breaks — statutory explained](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/consumer-rights-when-something-breaks/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-31. A manufacturer warranty is one layer of protection, but in many countries you have separate statutory rights against the seller that are not the same thing.
- [Warranty gotchas — the fine print that voids your cover](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/warranty-gotchas-fine-print/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-30. Many warranties contain clauses that void coverage under common, everyday conditions — improper use, unauthorised repairs, exposure to moisture, or even opening the device yourself.
- [Repair it or replace it? A simple way to decide](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/repair-it-or-replace-it/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-30. When something breaks, the repair quote often lands in an awkward middle ground — expensive enough to make you hesitate, cheap enough that replacement feels like waste.
- [How to organise receipts so you can actually find them](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-to-organise-receipts/) — organizing, 2026-07-30. Keeping receipts doesn't require a filing system or a weekend project.
- [How to make a warranty claim (and what to do when it's refused)](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-to-make-a-warranty-claim/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-30. A warranty only pays out if you know how to use it.
- [How long is the warranty on common things — a plain reference](https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-long-is-the-warranty-on-common-things/) — warranty-tips, 2026-07-30. Most products carry a standard one-year manufacturer warranty, but some categories vary widely — large appliances often two to five years, tyres are covered by tread-wear programs, and mattresses carry anything from two to twenty depending on the brand.
